verses.text: It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to Yahweh your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments which I command you today, that Yahweh your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to Yahweh your God’s voice.
You shall be blessed in the city, and you shall be blessed in the field.
You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock.
Your basket and your kneading trough shall be blessed.
You shall be blessed when you come in, and you shall be blessed when you go out.
Yahweh will cause your enemies who rise up against you to be struck before you. They will come out against you one way, and will flee before you seven ways.
Yahweh will command the blessing on you in your barns, and in all that you put your hand to. He will bless you in the land which Yahweh your God gives you.
Yahweh will establish you for a holy people to himself, as he has sworn to you, if you shall keep the commandments of Yahweh your God, and walk in his ways.
All the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by Yahweh’s name, and they will be afraid of you.
Yahweh will grant you abundant prosperity, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers to give you.
Yahweh will open to you his good treasure in the sky, to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, and you will not borrow.

Yahweh will make you the head, and not the tail. You will be above only, and you will not be beneath; if you listen to the commandments of Yahweh your God, which I command you today, to observe and to do,
and shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you today, to the right hand, or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

But it shall come to pass, if you will not listen to Yahweh your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command you today, that all these curses will come on you, and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city, and you will be cursed in the field.
Your basket and your kneading trough will be cursed.
The fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock will be cursed.
You will be cursed when you come in, and you will be cursed when you go out.

Yahweh will send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke, in all that you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed, and until you perish quickly; because of the evil of your doings, by which you have forsaken me.
Yahweh will make the pestilence cling to you, until he has consumed you from off the land, where you go in to possess it.
Yahweh will strike you with consumption, with fever, with inflammation, with fiery heat, with the sword, with blight, and with mildew. They will pursue you until you perish.
Your sky that is over your head will be brass, and the earth that is under you will be iron.
Yahweh will make the rain of your land powder and dust. It will come down on you from the sky, until you are destroyed.

Yahweh will cause you to be struck before your enemies. You will go out one way against them, and will flee seven ways before them. You will be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead body will be food to all birds of the sky, and to the animals of the earth; and there will be no one to frighten them away.
Yahweh will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with the tumors, with the scurvy, and with the itch, of which you can not be healed.
Yahweh will strike you with madness, with blindness, and with astonishment of heart.
You will grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways. You will only be oppressed and robbed always, and there will be no one to save you.
You will betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her. You will build a house, and you won’t dwell in it. You will plant a vineyard, and not use its fruit.

Your ox will be slain before your eyes, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be violently taken away from before your face, and will not be restored to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people. Your eyes will look, and fail with longing for them all day long. There will be no power in your hand.
A nation which you don’t know eat the fruit of your ground and all of your work. You will only be oppressed and crushed always;
so that the sights that you see with your eyes will drive you mad.
Yahweh will strike you in the knees and in the legs with a sore boil, of which you can not be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
Yahweh will bring you, and your king whom you will set over yourselves, to a nation that you have not known, you nor your fathers. There you will serve other gods of wood and stone.
You will become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples where Yahweh will lead you away.
You will carry much seed out into the field, and will gather little in; for the locust will consume it.
You will plant vineyards and dress them, but you will neither drink of the wine, nor harvest, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you won’t anoint yourself with the oil; for your olives will drop off.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours; for they will go into captivity.
Locusts will consume all of your trees and the fruit of your ground.
The foreigner who is among you will mount up above you higher and higher, and you will come down lower and lower.
He will lend to you, and you won’t lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come on you, and will pursue you, and overtake you, until you are destroyed; because you didn’t listen to Yahweh your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you.
They will be for a sign and for a wonder to you and to your offspring  forever.
Because you didn’t serve Yahweh your God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;
therefore you will serve your enemies whom Yahweh sends against you, in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in lack of all things. He will put an iron yoke on your neck, until he has destroyed you.
Yahweh will bring a nation against you from far, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies; a nation whose language you will not understand;
a nation of fierce facial expressions, that doesn’t respect the elderly, nor show favor to the young,

and they will eat the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground, until you are destroyed. They also won’t leave you grain, new wine, or oil, the increase of your livestock, or the young of your flock, until they have caused you to perish.

They will besiege you in all your gates, until your high and fortified walls come down, in which you trusted, throughout all your land. They will besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land, which Yahweh your God has given you.
You will eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters, whom Yahweh your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemies will distress you.
The man who is tender among you, and very delicate, his eye will be evil toward his brother, toward the wife whom he loves, and toward the remnant of his children whom he has remaining;

so that he will not give to any of them of the flesh of his children whom he will eat, because he has nothing left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in all your gates.

The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicateness and tenderness, her eye will be evil toward the husband that she loves, toward her son, toward her daughter,

toward her young one who comes out from between her feet, and toward her children whom she bears; for she will eat them secretly for lack of all things, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in your gates.
If you will not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that you may fear this glorious and fearful name, YAHWEH YOUR GOD;
then Yahweh will make your plagues fearful, and the plagues of your offspring,  even great plagues, and of long duration, and severe sicknesses, and of long duration.
He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of; and they will cling to you.
Also every sickness and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, Yahweh will bring them on you, until you are destroyed.
You will be left few in number, even though you were as the stars of the sky for multitude; because you didn’t listen to Yahweh your God’s voice.

It will happen that as Yahweh rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so Yahweh will rejoice over you to cause you to perish, and to destroy you. You will be plucked from off of the land where you go in to possess it.

Yahweh will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There you will serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor your fathers, even wood and stone.
Among these nations you will find no ease, and there will be no rest for the sole of your foot; but Yahweh will give you there a trembling heart, failing of eyes, and pining of soul.
Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day, and will have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you will say, “I wish it were evening!” and at evening you will say, “I wish it were morning!” for the fear of your heart which you will fear, and for the sights which your eyes will see.

Yahweh will bring you into Egypt again with ships, by the way of which I told to you that you would never see it again. There you will sell yourselves to your enemies for male and female slaves, and nobody will buy you.

footnotes.content: Moses sets out the offer plain as daylight: listen to the Lord's voice, and He will place you highest among nations. It's not about earning His favor—it's about aligning ourselves with the way He made things to work. Obedience opens the door to blessing; it doesn't buy it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "All these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you." What a picture—blessings chasing you down like someone running to catch up. The Lord doesn't measure His gifts by degree; He lets them overflow, pressing in from all sides.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: City and field—the whole span of a person's life, the places where we work and rest. Blessing doesn't favor one over the other; it follows you everywhere you actually live. That steadiness was what Israel needed to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals." Life multiplies—children, crops, livestock—and all of it is held as a gift. In a land they'd receive, these would be the signs that the Lord keeps His promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The basket and kneading trough—humble tools of daily bread. The Lord blesses not just the grand things, but the small rituals of home. A blessed kitchen table says He cares for the whole of us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Blessed when you come in, and blessed when you go out." Every threshold, every departure, every return—the Lord's watch covers it all. There's something deeply reassuring about knowing you're guarded at every turning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Enemies strike before you, but they flee seven ways—overwhelming rout, complete reversal. Moses is telling them: you won't fight alone. The Lord Himself will scatter what rises against you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord commands blessing into your barns, into all your hands touch. This isn't automatic; it's His active word working in your work. When you build, plant, or gather, He's not watching from a distance—He's speaking life into it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Establish you for a holy people." Holy means set apart—not for superiority, but for belonging to the Lord alone, walking in His ways. The whole covenant hinges on this one choice: Will you be His?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The peoples of the earth see you are called by His name—you bear His label, His reputation rides on you. With that honor comes a weight: you represent Him to the watching world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abundant prosperity—children, flocks, land—flowing out of the swearing the Lord made to their fathers. These aren't new promises; they're old promises kept, generation after generation, if the line stays faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Open to you his good treasure in the sky." Rain in its season was life itself in that land. Lending to many, not borrowing—the image flips the natural order: the blessed become the generous, not the needful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Head, not tail; above, not beneath. Moses isn't promising dominion to puff them up—he's saying: obedience lifts. You choose who you serve, and that choice determines where you stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't turn aside—not right, not left. Straight ahead is the only path that holds the promise. Even a small step toward another god tips the balance; faithfulness demands unwavering attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The pivot. If you won't listen—if you turn from His commandments—then all these curses come on you like the blessings came. The logic is plain: reject the Source of life, and life itself becomes hostile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursed in the city, cursed in the field—mirror image of blessing. Nowhere is safe; the Lord's hand can reach you anywhere. It's meant to be stark, to shake you awake before you wander too far.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The basket and kneading trough turn cursed—the very tools that fed you now become signs of emptiness. Where there was bread, there's hunger. The familiar becomes the witness against you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fruit of body, ground, livestock—everything that multiplies is now sterile. It's not just hardship; it's the reversal of all a person works toward. Life withers instead of flourishes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursed coming in, cursed going out—no threshold is safe. Every door you open, every journey you take, you carry the weight of alienation from the God who kept you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursing, confusion, rebuke—the Lord doesn't withdraw silently. He actively works against what you build because you've already worked against Him. And the reason is personal: you forsook Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pestilence clings until you're consumed—disease not as accident, but as consequence. The Lord shows no preference for the unfaithful; He lets them taste the fruit they've sown.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Consumption, fever, inflammation, sword, blight, mildew—sickness and ruin from every angle. There's no escape door, no corner where the curse doesn't reach. It pursues like an enemy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Your sky will be brass, and the earth under you will be iron." No rain, no softness, no mercy from creation itself. Heaven becomes impenetrable, the ground becomes unyielding—nature speaks judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rain becomes powder and dust—the blessing inverted, a choking fog instead of life-giving water. Everything meant to nourish becomes suffocating.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You go out one way against enemies but flee seven ways—total rout, absolute loss. And then exile: tossed among kingdoms, a stranger without rest. The reversal of blessing is complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dead lie unburied, food to birds and beasts—the final indignity in that culture. Even in death, no dignity, no honor, no one to care for you. It's the ultimate isolation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Boils, tumors, scurvy, itch—the flesh itself becomes a place of torment, and no healing comes. Your own body becomes evidence of separation from the God who made it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Madness, blindness, astonishment of heart—the mind and spirit break under the weight. You become lost to yourself, unable to think clearly, unable to see the way home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Groping in daylight like the blind—you stumble through ordinary time with no orientation. Nothing prospers; you're robbed always, with no rescuer. It's relentless, unending.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You betroth a wife but another takes her; you build but don't dwell; you plant but don't harvest. Everything you reach for slips away—the pattern of loss and theft and emptiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your animals slain, stolen, given to enemies—your livelihood, your wealth, stripped from you while you watch. And no one rescues you because you've already abandoned the One who alone could.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your children given to another people; you watch them, longing, helpless. No tragedy cuts deeper than the loss of your own young to strangers. And your hands hold no power to bring them back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A people you don't know eat the fruit of your labor; you're crushed and oppressed always. You work, but the stranger keeps. It's the ultimate inversion of the blessing you rejected.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sights you see drive you mad—watching the reversal of everything, the fulfillment of every threat. The mind can't bear it; reason fractures under the weight of loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sore boils from foot to crown—no part of you escapes; no healing comes. You live in chronic pain, visible and incurable, a walking sign of the curse.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yahweh will bring you to a nation that you have not known." This isn't just hardship—it's exile, uprooting from the land of promise. And there you serve other gods, enslaved to false worship in a foreign place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An astonishment, a proverb, a byword—you become the cautionary tale, the reference point for shame. Your name, your story, is used by others to warn about the cost of turning from God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You carry much seed to the field but the locust eats it all—labor without reward, hope without fruition. Everything you invest is consumed before you can harvest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You plant and tend vineyards but worms eat them; you drink no wine. Even the vintage, the sweetness, is taken from you. Care means nothing; ruin wins anyway.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Olive trees throughout your borders, but you won't anoint yourself—the oil, the sign of joy and blessing, never reaches you. Abundance sits all around you, but you can't touch it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sons and daughters born to you, but they go into captivity—they're not yours to keep. The deepest hurt a parent knows: watching your children torn away to slavery.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Locusts consume every tree and fruit—nothing survives. The land itself becomes hostile, stripped bare by the Lord's judgment working through creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The foreigner mounts above you higher and higher; you descend lower and lower. The hierarchy inverts completely. You become subject to those you might have led.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The foreigner lends to you; you don't lend to him. He's the head; you're the tail—the final summary. Every blessing of abundance you rejected becomes the foreigner's; you're left only needful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All these curses come on you, pursue you, overtake you, until destruction. The reason stands plain: you didn't listen, didn't keep His commandments. It's not random; it's the consequence of choice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These curses become a sign and wonder to you and your offspring forever—your family remembers them, teaches them. The story of your disobedience is passed down as testimony.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You didn't serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness, even amid abundance. You had everything and your heart was still somewhere else—that's the real sin beneath the sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Therefore you'll serve your enemies in hunger, thirst, nakedness, lack. The iron yoke you refused from the Lord—you wear it for men instead. False service always enslaves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A nation from far, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies." Ruthless conquest, swift and inevitable as a bird of prey. The Lord brings judgment from a place you can't defend against.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fierce expressions, no respect for age or youth—a people without mercy or family feeling. They come with neither pity nor restraint, and you'll know what it means to face judgment without a shield.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They eat the fruit of your livestock and ground until you're destroyed; they leave you no grain, wine, oil—nothing. Complete devastation, famine imposed by conquerors who strip you bare.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Besieged in all your gates; your high walls come down. The fortifications you trusted fail. You're trapped, surrounded, the city itself becomes your prison.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You eat the flesh of your own children in siege and distress—the unthinkable horror, the breaking of every law of nature. Desperation destroys the last bonds of love and kinship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tender, delicate man—his eye becomes evil toward his brother, his wife, his children. Starvation hardens the heart; love becomes suspicion when survival's at stake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He won't share the flesh of his children—he eats in secret, alone, out of sheer desperation and isolation. The family bond shatters; everyone fends for themselves in the darkness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tender woman—she wouldn't set her foot on the ground for delicacy—becomes driven by the same evil eye, the same hunger. Refinement means nothing; survival strips away all dignity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She eats her newborn in secret—the deepest horror, motherhood inverted. Even the newborn—the most innocent—isn't safe. The curse has broken everything sacred.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "If you will not observe all the words of this law." Not some, not the parts you like—all of it. The law isn't a menu; it's the whole structure of covenant. Half-obedience is disobedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Plagues fearful, great and long-lasting, sicknesses severe and long—not quick suffering, but prolonged torment. The Lord makes sure you understand the weight of your choice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He brings on you again all the diseases of Egypt—echoing the plagues that freed you, now used as judgment against you. What once was a sign of liberation becomes a sign of judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every sickness and plague not even written in the law—the list is endless. The Lord's judgment isn't limited to what was warned; it exceeds imagination. He can do more than He promised to do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You'll be few in number, though once like the stars—the multiplication promised is reversed. The Lord brought you from nothing to multitude; He can reduce you back to nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As the Lord rejoiced to do you good and multiply you, so He'll rejoice to cause you to perish and destroy you. The same energy, the same delight in action, now turned to judgment. It's not indifference; it's active reversal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Scattered among all peoples from one end of the earth to the other—diaspora, uprooting complete. You serve other gods, wood and stone, in lands you never knew. Total dispersion and spiritual captivity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No ease, no rest for your foot—wandering without settlement. The Lord gives you a trembling heart, failing eyes, pining soul. Even your inner being is broken; nothing steadies you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your life hangs in doubt; you're afraid night and day, with no assurance. Life becomes a fragile thing, held by a thread you can't control, lived in constant fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "In the morning you will say, 'I wish it were evening,' and at evening, 'I wish it were morning.'" Readers today hear an echo of what happens when we run from the One who anchors us—the restlessness that chases the human soul. We trade His peace for a treadmill of wishing our lives away. As of 2026-10, I've seen it: unfaith exhausts in a way faithfulness never does.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You go back to Egypt by ship—back to bondage, the place you were freed from. You'll sell yourselves as slaves, and nobody will buy you—not even worth the price of a slave. The circle is complete; you've undone the Exodus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
